Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice, Turkey's Best 2024, 2025

venues.name: Raffles Istanbul
venues.note: Glamorous, art-filled and high above the city, with Raffles' signature service and a view to the strait.

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental Bosphorus, Istanbul
venues.note: A calm seaside retreat on the European shore, the group's quiet precision, with the water at the door.

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Istanbul
venues.note: A polished city tower above Dolmabahçe with sweeping Bosphorus vistas from the upper floors.

venues.name: The St. Regis Istanbul
venues.note: Art Deco glamour in the middle of the city's smartest shopping district, with the signature butler on every stay.

venues.name: Park Hyatt Istanbul – Maçka Palas
venues.note: An updated 1920s Italianate palazzo, discreet, design-led and steps from the boutiques.

venues.name: JW Marriott Hotel Istanbul Marmara Sea
venues.note: A stylish seaside skyscraper on the Marmara, with a marina and long sea views.

venues.name: Six Senses Kocataş Mansions Istanbul
venues.note: Two restored 19th-century mansions on the upper Bosphorus, a wellness-led urban resort away from the crowds.

venues.name: The Bank Hotel Istanbul
venues.note: A grand old bank in Karaköy, reborn as a sharp, contemporary house in the city's most creative quarter.

venues.name: AJWA Sultanahmet
venues.note: An Ottoman-Seljuk fantasy in the old city, richly detailed and warmly, traditionally run.

venues.name: Ecole St. Pierre Hotel
venues.note: A restored historic school turned intimate design hotel, in the thick of Galata.

venues.name: Pera Palace Hotel
venues.note: The Orient Express hotel of 1895, Agatha Christie's rooms and a century of Istanbul history intact.

venues.name: Fairmont Quasar Istanbul
venues.note: A landmark tower on a restored heritage base, polished, central and generously scaled.

venues.name: Conrad Istanbul Bosphorus
venues.note: A refreshed modern house above the strait, reliable, spacious and quietly capable.

venues.name: Bebek Hotel by The Stay
venues.note: A tiny waterfront boutique in the city's most fashionable village, right on the Bebek promenade.

venues.name: Address Istanbul
venues.note: A contemporary high-rise with skyline views and the group's slick, service-led ease.

venues.name: Soho House Istanbul
venues.note: A 19th-century Italianate palazzo turned members'-club-and-hotel, the address of the creative crowd.

venues.name: The Stay Bosphorus
venues.note: A slim design house on the waterfront at Ortaköy, under the shadow of the bridge.

venues.name: TURK Fatih Tutak
venues.note: The city's sole two-star, Fatih Tutak's radical, refined reimagining of Anatolian cooking.

venues.name: Mikla
venues.note: Turkish ingredients through a Scandinavian lens, on a rooftop with the whole old city laid out below.

venues.name: Neolokal
venues.note: Heritage Anatolian dishes reborn as contemporary art, tradition, plated for today.

venues.name: Nicole
venues.note: French-influenced Turkish refinement in a historic Pera mansion, elegant, exacting, personal.

venues.name: Araka
venues.note: A garden restaurant on the upper Bosphorus where modern Turkish cooking feels both familiar and new.

venues.name: Arkestra
venues.note: A progressive tasting menu that ranges the globe while staying rooted in Istanbul's energy.

venues.name: Sankai by Nagaya
venues.note: A minimalist Japanese haven and flawless omakase, a meditative break from the city's noise.

venues.name: Araf İstanbul
venues.note: A pocket-sized Asian-shore kitchen doing contemporary Turkish cooking over coals, newly starred.

venues.name: Alaf
venues.note: Nomadic Anatolian traditions and wood-fired cooking, done with real intent.

venues.name: Aman da Bravo
venues.note: Refined Turkish cooking with a quiet gastronomic ambition, at a price that flatters it.

venues.name: Aheste
venues.note: Small plates of modern Turkish with a lightness of touch, a Pera favourite.

venues.name: Cuma
venues.note: A relaxed all-day room in antique-lined Çukurcuma, Mediterranean-Turkish cooking, done simply and well.

venues.name: Karaköy Lokantası
venues.note: A beloved tiled meyhane serving the classics of Istanbul cooking, meze by day, raki tables by night.

venues.name: Giritli
venues.note: A set-menu Cretan-Aegean seafood feast in a walled old-city garden, meze that keeps coming.

venues.name: Tersane
venues.note: Traditional meze and charcoal-grilled meats in the old shipyard quarter, honest and full-flavoured.

venues.name: Pandeli
venues.note: A turquoise-tiled institution above the Spice Bazaar, serving Ottoman classics since 1901.

venues.name: Sade Beş Denizler Mutfağı
venues.note: Anatolian cooking drawn from Türkiye's five seas, regional dishes rarely seen on a city menu.

venues.name: Calipso
venues.note: Meze and Aegean seafood on the Anatolian side, a locals' favourite worth the crossing.

venues.name: Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya)
venues.note: The single building that explains Istanbul: a 6th-century Byzantine cathedral, then imperial mosque, then museum, now a working mosque again, its vast gold-flecked dome still floating over the nave. Go early to feel the scale before the crowds; the surviving Christian mosaics in the upper galleries are worth the climb.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque)
venues.note: Facing Hagia Sophia across a garden, this is the great cascade of half-domes and six minarets, its interior sheathed in more than 20,000 hand-painted Iznik tiles that give it its blue glow. Freshly restored, it remains an active mosque, dress modestly and time your visit outside prayer hours.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Topkapı Palace
venues.note: Home to the Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries, a series of courtyards, tiled pavilions and treasuries that reward slow wandering. Buy the separate Harem ticket, see the Imperial Treasury and the sacred relics, and pause at the terrace above Seraglio Point for the Bosphorus view. A private guide makes the layered history land for a multi-generational family.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı)
venues.note: Descend into a cathedral-like underground reservoir built under Justinian, 336 columns rising from dark water with the famous carved Medusa heads at the base of two of them. Restored and atmospherically lit, it is cool, hushed and short, an easy, memorable stop between the big monuments.

venues.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
venues.note: The masterpiece of the great architect Sinan and the finest of Istanbul's imperial mosques, calmer and more crowd-free than the Blue Mosque, crowning a hill with a sweeping terrace over the Golden Horn. The tomb-garden holds Süleyman the Magnificent and his wife Roxelana; nearby lanes hide old teahouses.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Grand Bazaar (Kapalı Çarşı)
venues.note: One of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, thousands of shops under painted vaults, each lane once dedicated to a trade: gold, carpets, ceramics, antiques, leather. For serious buyers, the discreet dealers in the old Cevahir Bedesten (the inner hall) hold the finest antique jewellery and objects; a trusted guide gets you past the tourist stalls.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı)
venues.note: The L-shaped 17th-century market by the waterfront, piled with saffron, dried fruit, nuts, teas, lokum and pyramids of spice. Smaller and more sensory than the Grand Bazaar, pick up pistachio baklava and Turkish delight, and slip into the surrounding streets for the city's best coffee and cheese merchants.

venues.name: Bosphorus by private yacht
venues.note: The essential Istanbul experience: gliding the strait that divides Europe and Asia, past Ottoman waterfront mansions (yalıs), the fortresses, Dolmabahçe and Ortaköy, under the suspension bridges. A chartered yacht at golden hour, with a discreet crew and a private table, is the version a discerning family remembers.

venues.name: Dolmabahçe Palace
venues.note: The Ottomans' answer to Versailles on the European shore, 285 rooms of crystal, gold leaf and the world's largest Bohemian chandelier, where the empire's last sultans lived and Atatürk died. The ceremonial halls and the waterfront gardens are the highlight; go by boat for the full effect.

venues.name: Chora Church / Kariye Mosque (Kariye Camii)
venues.note: A modest exterior hiding the greatest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, luminous cycles of the life of Christ and the Virgin across every vault and dome. Out near the old land walls, it rewards the detour; recently reopened after long restoration.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Galata Tower
venues.note: The 14th-century Genoese watchtower that anchors the Galata skyline; the top balcony gives a full 360° sweep across the old city, the Golden Horn and the Bosphorus. Best at sunset, book ahead to skip the line, then wander down through the steep, gallery-lined streets below.

venues.name: İstiklal Avenue & Beyoğlu
venues.note: The grand pedestrian spine of modern Istanbul, running from Taksim to Galata past belle-époque arcades, patisseries, bookshops and the nostalgic red tram. Duck into the side streets, Asmalımescit, Çukurcuma, Cihangir, for the antique shops, wine bars and cafés where the city's creative class actually spends its evenings.

venues.name: Balat & Fener
venues.note: The photogenic old Greek and Jewish quarters on the Golden Horn, rainbow terraced houses on steep lanes, antique dealers, third-wave cafés and the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate. The most atmospheric neighbourhood in the city to simply wander a morning with a camera.

venues.name: Kadıköy (Asian side)
venues.note: Take the ferry across for the real, unhurried Istanbul, the Kadıköy market quarter is one of the city's best food districts, dense with fishmongers, spice stalls, meze counters and meyhanes. Strong on vegetarian meze too; a food walk here beats any tourist restaurant across the water.

venues.name: Istanbul Archaeological Museums
venues.note: A three-museum complex just below Topkapı holding treasures like the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Ishtar Gate tiles and antiquities from across the former Ottoman lands. Uncrowded and beautifully laid out, a serious hour for anyone who wants depth beyond the mosques.

venues.name: Istanbul Modern
venues.note: Türkiye's leading modern and contemporary art museum, reborn in a striking Renzo Piano building on the Bosphorus waterfront with a rooftop terrace and reflecting pool. Strong Turkish collection, ambitious temporary shows and one of the best design shops in the city.

venues.name: Pera Museum
venues.note: An elegant private museum in a former grand hotel, best known for Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer' and a fine collection of Orientalist painting, alongside Anatolian weights and Kütahya tiles. Manageable in size, thoughtfully curated, with a lovely café.

venues.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum
venues.note: A waterfront mansion museum up the Bosphorus with world-class Ottoman calligraphy and painting, blockbuster travelling exhibitions, and gardens over the strait. Its restaurant, MSA, is a destination in itself, an easy, refined half-day for a family, paired with Emirgan Park next door.

venues.name: Museum of Innocence
venues.note: Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk's novel made physical, a townhouse of vitrines filled with the everyday objects of 1970s Istanbul, from cigarette stubs to hairpins, telling a love story object by object. Quietly moving and unlike any other museum in the world; bring the book's ticket page for free entry.

venues.name: Rüstem Paşa Mosque
venues.note: A hidden jewel above the Spice Bazaar's warehouses, a small Sinan mosque wrapped inside and out in the most exquisite Iznik tiles in the city, tomato-red and turquoise. Easy to miss and rarely crowded; a real connoisseur's stop between the bigger sights.

venues.name: Süleymaniye view & backstreets
venues.note: Beyond the mosque itself, the old quarter of wooden houses, ateliers and the classic çorba (bean-stew) houses is one of the last authentically Ottoman neighbourhoods, and the terrace beside the mosque is arguably the finest free viewpoint over the Golden Horn.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı
venues.note: A 16th-century Sinan-built bath, meticulously restored, offering the classic marble-slab scrub-and-foam ritual in a soaring domed hall. Well-run and refined, the most tasteful introduction to the hammam for first-timers, with separate men's and women's sessions.

venues.name: Çağaloğlu Hamamı
venues.note: One of the last great classical Ottoman baths, built in 1741, with a guest list running from Florence Nightingale to Kaiser Wilhelm II. Grand marble interiors and a full menu of scrubs and massages, an atmospheric, historic hammam a short walk from Hagia Sophia.

venues.name: Ortaköy waterfront & mosque
venues.note: The little baroque mosque on the water, framed dead-on by the great suspension bridge, is one of Istanbul's signature views, especially at sunset. The square behind it is a lively weekend scene of cafés, an antiques-and-crafts market and the famous stuffed-baked-potato (kumpir) stalls.

venues.name: Gülhane Park
venues.note: The oldest public park in the city, the former outer gardens of Topkapı, ablaze with tulips in spring and shaded by old planes year-round. A calm green pause between the monuments, with a cliff-top tea garden looking over the Bosphorus at the far end.

venues.name: Emirgan Park
venues.note: A hillside grove of restored Ottoman pavilions and formal gardens up the European shore, and the heart of the city's April Tulip Festival with millions of blooms. Genuinely family-friendly and unhurried, pair it with the Sabancı Museum next door.

venues.name: Galata Mevlevihanesi (Whirling Dervishes)
venues.note: The city's oldest Mevlevi lodge, now a museum, where a genuine sema ceremony, the meditative whirling of the Sufi dervishes, is performed to live ney music. Small, ticketed and reverent; the real thing rather than the dinner-show imitations elsewhere.

venues.name: Çiçek Pasajı & Balık Pazarı
venues.note: A glass-roofed 19th-century arcade of historic meyhanes off İstiklal, spilling into the atmospheric fish market lanes behind, the classic setting for an evening of meze, grilled fish and raki with live fasıl music. Touristy but genuinely fun; the deeper backstreet meyhanes are where locals go.

venues.name: Rahmi M. Koç Museum
venues.note: Türkiye's great museum of industry and transport on the Golden Horn, restored trams, vintage cars, aircraft, a real submarine you can board, and hands-on exhibits. The most child- and grandchild-friendly museum in Istanbul, with a good waterside restaurant.

venues.name: Çamlıca Hill & Grand Çamlıca Mosque
venues.note: The highest hill on the Asian side, with the classic panorama over the whole city, the Bosphorus and the Marmara, clear enough on a good day to see the Princes' Islands. Beside it stands the vast Grand Çamlıca Mosque, the largest in Türkiye, worth seeing for sheer scale.

venues.name: Pierre Loti Hill & Eyüp Sultan Mosque
venues.note: Ride the little cable car up to the café named for the French novelist for one of the loveliest views down the Golden Horn, then descend to Eyüp Sultan, one of Islam's holiest sites in Türkiye and a deeply local pilgrimage quarter far from the tourist trail.

venues.name: Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi)
venues.note: The tiny islet tower marooned at the mouth of the Bosphorus, wrapped in legend and lately restored, reachable by a short boat hop from Üsküdar or Kabataş. More postcard than must-see, but the café terrace gives a rare view back at the old-city skyline from the water.

venues.name: Çukurcuma antique quarter
venues.note: A steep warren of streets packed with antique dealers, vintage furniture, old maps, textiles and curiosities, the place serious collectors and interior people spend an afternoon. Cluster your browsing on Faik Paşa and Çukur Cuma streets, then coffee in Cihangir up the hill.

venues.name: Yıldız Park & pavilions
venues.note: A wooded royal park climbing the hillside above the Bosphorus, dotted with delicate late-Ottoman kiosks and greenhouses, once the private grounds of Sultan Abdülhamid II. Quiet, green and uncrowded, a good-weather escape with tea in a historic pavilion.

venues.name: Little Hagia Sophia (Küçük Ayasofya Camii)
venues.note: A serene 6th-century Byzantine church-turned-mosque, once a model for its far larger namesake, with a beautiful two-storey colonnade and an intimate, worshipful calm. A short walk down from the Blue Mosque and blissfully free of crowds.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Hippodrome / Sultanahmet Square
venues.note: The long public square that was the chariot-racing arena of Byzantine Constantinople, still marked by the Egyptian Obelisk, the bronze Serpent Column and the German Fountain. Walk it between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque and the layers of two empires line up in a single open space.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul

venues.name: Arasta Bazaar
venues.note: The small, calm arcade of shops tucked behind the Blue Mosque, originally built to fund it, good-quality carpets, ceramics and textiles without the Grand Bazaar's hustle. The best place near the monuments to shop at a civilised pace; the little Mosaic Museum sits right alongside.

venues.name: Great Palace Mosaic Museum
venues.note: A single dazzling survival of Byzantine Constantinople, the vast floor mosaics of the vanished Great Palace of the emperors, teeming with hunting scenes and everyday life, displayed in situ. Small, extraordinary and overlooked, right off the Arasta Bazaar.

venues.name: Rumeli Fortress (Rumeli Hisarı)
venues.note: The dramatic mid-15th-century fortress Mehmed the Conqueror threw up in four months to strangle Byzantine Constantinople, its towers climbing straight from the Bosphorus shore. Great ramparts to explore, and the surrounding waterfront of Bebek and Rumeli Hisarı is prime café territory.

venues.name: Bebek waterfront
venues.note: Istanbul's most moneyed shoreline, a curve of Bosphorus bay lined with mansions, moored yachts and the city society's favourite cafés and restaurants. Come for a long, unhurried breakfast or waterside coffee and watch the city's smart set at ease.

venues.name: Suna & İnan Kıraç Kadıköy / Nişantaşı shopping
venues.note: Istanbul's luxury retail district, Abdi İpekçi Caddesi and its side streets carry the international houses alongside the best Turkish designers, jewellers and concept stores. The natural base for discreet, appointment-led personal shopping, with elegant cafés between.

venues.name: Princes' Islands (Büyükada)
venues.note: A ferry hop out to a car-free island of pine woods, Belle Époque villas and sea views, you get around on foot, bicycle or electric cart. Lunch by the harbour, wander the mansion-lined lanes, and Istanbul suddenly feels a world away; an easy, gentle day for all ages.

venues.name: Polonezköy
venues.note: A leafy village founded by 19th-century Polish émigrés in the forests north-east of the city, a rare pocket of quiet, walking trails and long country lunches of pork and homemade preserves. An unusual, restful escape from the metropolis, popular for weekend brunch.

venues.name: Edirne (Selimiye Mosque)
venues.note: The former Ottoman capital near the Greek and Bulgarian borders, home to Sinan's crowning masterpiece, the Selimiye Mosque, the architect's own declared finest work, its dome engineered to rival Hagia Sophia's. A serious architectural pilgrimage for those who want the definitive Ottoman monument.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Selimiye Mosque and its Social Complex

venues.name: Mikla (rooftop bar)
venues.note: Sunset drinks above the whole old city, atop the Marmara Pera, the rooftop attached to one of Istanbul's great restaurants.
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)

venues.name: Bebek Hotel rooftop bar
venues.note: A mid-century landmark on the Bebek waterfront, cocktails at the water's edge in the city's most fashionable village.
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)

venues.name: Alexandra Cocktail Bar
venues.note: A historic Bosphorus house turned serious cocktail address, with a rooftop over the strait and a bartender in the 50 Best Bars Academy.
credentials: Genuine standing, Osman Fethi Baycan, The World's 50 Best Bars Academy (Türkiye)

venues.name: Fahri Konsolos
venues.note: The Asian shore's most inventive bar, house liquors, bitters and infusions built on Anatolian ingredients like sumac and pomegranate molasses.
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)

venues.name: 360 Istanbul
venues.note: The rooftop that named the genre, a full 360° sweep of Bosphorus, Golden Horn and Sultanahmet from one terrace.
credentials: Genuine standing, Istanbul's original and best-known Beyoğlu rooftop

venues.name: Asmalı Cavit
venues.note: The meyhane other meyhanes are measured against, rakı, meze and long tables where strangers become regulars.
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)

venues.name: Muuto
venues.note: Chef Umut Karakuş's Anatolian small-plates bar, colourful meze made for sharing over a long, loud table.
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)

venues.name: Çırağan Palace Kempinski, Bosphorus terrace bar
venues.note: A drink on the terrace of a restored imperial palace, the Bosphorus lit and moving at your feet, the city's grandest nightcap.
credentials: Genuine standing, Çırağan Palace Kempinski (Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star; The Leading Hotels of the World)

venues.name: Pera Palace, Orient Bar
venues.note: A cocktail inside the 1895 Orient Express hotel, Agatha Christie's Istanbul, in wood, brass and low light.
credentials: Genuine standing, Pera Palace Hotel (Condé Nast Traveler, best hotels in Istanbul)
